title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC0LB_1RD0RC_1LA1RC_---1LF_1LB1LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC0LB_1RD0RC_1LA1RC_---1LF_1LB1LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and halting looks very unlikely. The tape is a list of blocks (1101)^n separated by single 0s. At each rest (head at the left end in state B) the tape is B>1 P (1101)^A 0 (1101)^b1 0 … with P = 0 or 000, and the list enters only through g = 6 + b1/2 + b2/4 + …. The next rest is A → (3A+g)/2 (with −3 or −6 for type 0), or, when the parity is wrong, a push: A+1 joins the list and A restarts at about (A+g)/4. This map reproduces all 36 rests of the direct run up to 1010 steps and 350 rests started from random configurations; it is built from sweep rules proved in Lean, but the map itself is not proved. Iterated 2·105 times from blank tape, A never comes near the tiny values from which the machine halts.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,407 cells have been visited and 27,448 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.542). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.14).

claims.title: Sweep rules of the transfer and counting phases
claims.text: Four rules from one moment the head is at the left end in state B reading 1 to the next, for every value of the counts: the transfer phase (two copies of 1101 leave the block left of the marker 00, three arrive right of it) and the counting phase with the marker next to the counter (the counter gains one while six copies cross the marker; at depth k it is 6·2k; depths 1, 2 and 3 are in lean/Deep.lean, below).

claims.title: Counting rules at depth 1, 2 and 3
claims.text: With one, two or three blocks between the counter and the block holding the marker, one unit of the counter costs 12, 24 or 48 copies of 1101 crossing the marker (8 + 4, 16 + 8, 32 + 16 in the two halves), for every value of the counts and any tape to the right. The mechanism: the block boundaries act as a binary counter, so the head makes 2k trips to the marker per unit at depth k. The rest map itself is still not proved.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A plain C simulator (longrun.c, on tools/c/tm.h) runs 1011 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end the head has visited cells -370,533 to 111 and 250,472 cells hold a 1.

claims.title: The rest map, checked against the machine
claims.text: With g = 6 + b1/2 + b2/4 + … (always an integer on the orbit, and A+g always a multiple of 3): type 000 goes to (3A+g)/2 when A+g is even, otherwise pushes A+1 and goes to type 000 with (A+g−5)/4 (A+g = 1 mod 4) or type 0 with (A+g+1)/4; type 0 goes to type 0 with (3A+g−3)/2 (A+g odd) or type 000 with (3A+g−6)/2. From type 0, A = 3, empty list (62 steps) it reproduces all 36 rests of the direct run up to 1010 steps, and the machine run from 350 random rests (A up to 600, lists of up to four blocks) reaches the predicted next rest every time.

claims.title: Where it halts
claims.text: Run from every rest with A < 40 and a list of at most two short blocks, the machine halts only from A = 0 with an empty list (type 0 or 000), after 91 steps, by the whole tape collapsing; the other small cases that leave the map involve blocks of length 1, which the orbit never creates once A > 1.

claims.title: The map iterated far, and the odds of a halt
claims.text: Iterated 2·10<sup>5</sup> times from blank tape, A stays at 64 or more from the 10th rest on and has 50,000 bits at the end (66,996 pushes). The size A+g is multiplied by 3/2 at every non-push rest and by about 3/4 at a push (a third of the rests): a random walk in log size with strong upward drift. Reaching size ~10 again from the 2·10<sup>4</sup> of the rest at 9.8·10<sup>9</sup> steps has probability of order 10<sup>−10</sup>; probviously non-halting.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would need the rest map for all values in Lean: the counting rule at every depth (an induction over the binary counter on the block boundaries), the marker crossing block boundaries mid-cycle, and the start and end phases. It would also need an argument that A+g never falls back to the handful of tiny configurations that halt, which is a Collatz-type question.

python3 holdouts/1RB0LE_1RC0LB_1RD0RC_1LA1RC_---1LF_1LB1LD/py/map.py random 200 11  # ... and against runs from random rests
python3 holdouts/1RB0LE_1RC0LB_1RD0RC_1LA1RC_---1LF_1LB1LD/py/map.py iterate 2e5   # the map from blank tape

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but it almost certainly never stops. This machine runs a Collatz-like rule: a number A on the tape is multiplied by 3/2 and topped up by a constant g that encodes a list of older numbers, and when the parity is wrong, A is filed away onto the list and a new, smaller A starts.

facts.text: The rest map, matching every rest of the run to 10<sup>10</sup> steps.
The map iterated from blank tape; A never small again.
The sweeps the map is built from (counting at depths 0 to 3, and transfer), proved for every count.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: A list of blocks and a marker
html: Between two rests the tape reads B>1 (1101)^c 0 (1101)^a 0 … (1101)^z 0 0 (1101)^y 0 …: a counter block c at the left, the list of blocks, and a marker 00 inside the list. Each round trip of the head moves copies of 1101 across the marker:

phasewhat one round trip doesproved
counting, depth kthe marker starts in the last block and moves left; 6·2k copies cross it per unit added to the counter (k = blocks between counter and marker)u0_* (depth 0)
transferthe counter, now a block of about 4c, loses 2 copies per half trip while the block right of the marker gains 3t_one, t_two

A block b at depth k adds about b/(6·2k) to the counter, and the transfer phase pays out 3/2 for each copy; together this is the map below, with the whole list summed up in one number g = 6 + b1/2 + b2/4 + ….

sections.heading: Multiply by 3/2, or file it away
html:
restconditionnext rest
type 000, AA+g eventype 000, (3A+g)/2
type 000, AA+g = 1 mod 4push A+1; type 000, (A+g−5)/4
type 000, AA+g = 3 mod 4push A+1; type 0, (A+g+1)/4
type 0, AA+g oddtype 0, (3A+g−3)/2
type 0, AA+g eventype 000, (3A+g−6)/2
A push puts the block A+1 at the front of the list, so g becomes (A+g+7)/2. From blank tape the first rest is type 0 with A = 3 and an empty list (g = 6):

Without a push the size A+g grows by half; a push (a third of the rests) shrinks it to about three quarters. The machine halts only from A = 0 with an empty list, so it would need this random-looking walk to come all the way back down; with the strong upward drift that has odds of order 10−10.

sections.heading: A binary counter hidden in the gaps
html: While the marker 00 works its way through the list, the single 0s between the blocks quietly become the bits of a binary counter. Each time the head comes back from the marker it looks at the gaps, deepest first. A gap showing 0 is set to 1 and the head turns back to the marker. A gap showing 1 is reset to 0 and the head keeps going: that is the carry. Only when the carry runs off the end does the counter at the left end go up by one.

blocks between counter and marker012k
trips to the marker per unit1242k
copies of 1101 moved per unit612246·2k

This is why block number k enters the map only through bk/2k. The rules for 0 to 3 blocks are proved in Lean. A proof for every k would go by induction over this counter, and it is the first missing piece of a proof of the whole map.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.542). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.14).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,407 cells (27,589 left of the start, 77 right), with a density of 1s of 0.734.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Antihydra-like: A → (3A+g)/2 or a push A → (A+g)/4 on a growing list of (1101)^n blocks, g = 6 + sum b_k/2^k
summary: An exact Collatz-like map on rests (A, g): A becomes (3A+g)/2, or the block is pushed onto a list (g := (A+g+7)/2) and A restarts near (A+g)/4; it matches every rest of the run to 1e10 steps, and halting needs A+g to fall back to single digits.
